rationale: Highest spectral anomaly in the event (RX 43707). The strongest signal gives laboratory analysis the best chance of identifying what is actually present.
expected_variables: Chlorophyll-a (spectrophotometric or HPLC); Total suspended solids (gravimetric); Turbidity (nephelometric, NTU); Phytoplankton identification and cell counts

rationale: Nearest analysable water to Annaba Port power station, 378 m away. This is the measurement that answers whether the asset is affected yet.
expected_variables: Turbidity (NTU); Chlorophyll-a; Total organic carbon; Algal toxins if a bloom is suspected

rationale: Edge of the event nearest the modelled drift direction (bearing 273deg). Sampling here tests whether the event is advancing and how sharp the front is.
expected_variables: Turbidity (NTU); Chlorophyll-a; Temperature and salinity profile

rationale: Lowest-anomaly water at least 800 m offshore (RX 1.2). Without a same-day control, an absolute laboratory value from the event cannot be interpreted.
expected_variables: Same analyte suite as the event core, for direct comparison

rationale: Marginal anomaly (RX between the 85th and 97th percentile) in shallow water, where bottom reflectance and suspended matter are hard to separate optically. A depth reading and a TSS sample here would resolve the ambiguity for the whole nearshore band.
expected_variables: Full analyte suite; Secchi depth; Water depth (to test bottom-reflectance influence)
